title: Theory Compendium: Social Interaction
text:
Symbolic interactionism focuses on how individuals create meaning through social contact and interpretation of symbols. This framework suggests that reality is not fixed but is collaboratively constructed in daily face-to-face exchanges.

A core element involves the concept of 'the looking glass self,' which posits that a person's sense of self is derived from their perception of how others view them. Consequently, social roles are understood as performances regulated by expectations and internalized norms within specific social settings.
